The Baltimore oriole (Icterus galbula) is a medium-sized icterid that undergoes a series of well-documented developmental transitions. During the early neonatal period, the altricial hatchlings are completely dependent on parental provisioning and have a recorded wet weight at birth of 2 grams [Wwb = 2 grams]. This modest initial mass is characteristic of icterid young, which exhibit a rapid growth trajectory fueled by a diet of caterpillars and other invertebrates provided by both parents.

The initial wet weight of a newly deposited egg, measured prior to the onset of significant embryonic development, has been documented at 2.99 grams [Ww0 = 2.99 grams], a value that correlates strongly with the provisioning capacity of the female and the eventual size of the hatchling.
